title: Constrained capacity pricing tilt + headcount staging (May 2025)
content:
Summary:
This worksheet drafts a compact playbook for a capacity-constrained pricing posture we are calling a "pricing tilt": small, staged price adjustments and headcount phasing intended to preserve unit margins during transient GPU capacity constraints or sudden cost-inflation events. The goal is to provide operational trigger rules and a shallow headcount staging plan (0–3 buckets) that can be executed quickly to change cash flow in the next 3–9 months without wholesale reorg.

Why this is different:
- Focuses on short-term, reversible levers (tilt pricing, temporary hiring hold, contract mix reweight) rather than long-term structural headcount cuts.
- Designed around capacity signals (GPU utilization by region, queue latency percentiles) rather than only revenue triggers.
- Creates a low-friction staging ladder that product and sales can communicate to customers.

Key assumptions (base case):
- ARR at review: $88M (run-rate).
- Avg tokens per hosted-request: 420 tokens; avg tokens per embedding call: 1,200 tokens.
- Current blended hosted per-token revenue: $0.00007 / token.
- Blended variable cost per token (GPU, networking, storage amortized): $0.000035 / token (50% margin).
- Dedicated/reserved revenue mix: 22% of revenue with higher gross margin (est. 68%).
- Capacity pressure scenario: spot GPU cost +30% vs baseline; queue P95 latency up 40% in us-west during peak.

Pricing Tilt Ladder (examples):
- Tilt A (low friction): +4% on non-enterprise public endpoints, apply immediately to new accounts; communicate as temporary surcharge tied to capacity pressure. Expected margin lift: +2–3 ppts.
- Tilt B (targeted): +8% on high-throughput API keys (top 10% by tokens), offers credit offsets for committed dedicated contracts. Expected margin lift: +4–6 ppts.
- Tilt C (aggressive): +12% on metered tiers if sustained capacity constraints >30 days, paired with optional temporary throughput caps for free-tier. Expected margin lift: +8–9 ppts.

Headcount staging (3 buckets) — intent: preserve critical product and SRE capacity while delaying lower-immediate-impact hiring:
- Bucket 0 (critical - hiring continues): Serving Runtime (kernel/latency team), SRE (oncall capacity), Security & Compliance (required for Private deals), Critical Platform Eng (autoscaling). Typical roles: 20 FTEs.
- Bucket 1 (deferable 1–3 months): Developer Experience (non-critical SDKs), Solutions Eng (pre-sales expansion hires), Research/Applied ML (new model experiments). Typical roles paused: 18 FTEs.
- Bucket 2 (deferable 3–9 months): GTM expansion (demand gen non-core roles), Facilities & Ops hires, some people ops hiring for long-term programs. Typical roles paused: 14 FTEs.
- Net hiring delta if full staging enacted: reduce planned H2 hires by ~52 FTEs (phased). Estimated monthly cash savings (ramp month): $1.3M–$1.8M depending on average comp assumptions.

Trigger rules (operational + financial) — triggers should be observable and automated where possible:
- Soft triggers (early warning): 10% month-over-month increase in P95 queue latency OR 12% monthly increase in spot GPU rate OR = 6% m/m decline in inbound trial-to-paid conversion. Action: enable Tilt A and pause Bucket 2 non-critical hiring.
- Hard triggers (action required within 7 days): sustained 30%+ spot GPU cost increase for 14 consecutive days OR P95 latency > target +40% and cannot be mitigated by routing. Action: enable Tilt B, pause Bucket 1, begin outreach to Dedicated prospects to accelerate high-margin sales.
- Emergency triggers (cash-protecting): runway drop projection to <10 months OR ARR churn spike >3ppt month-over-month. Action: enable Tilt C, hiring freeze across Buckets 1+2, evaluate temporary contractor conversion and two-week kills for discretionary spend.

Quick sensitivity table (textual) — modeled outcomes vs single-parameter shocks (illustrative):
- Spot GPU +30% w/o pricing tilt: gross margin drops 6–7 ppts; net cash burn +$1.6M/mo.
- Spot GPU +30% with Tilt A: gross margin -3–4 ppts; net cash burn +$0.6–0.9M/mo.
- Spot GPU +30% + Tilt B + pause Bucket 1 hires: gross margin ~baseline; net cash burn neutral to small +$0.1M/mo.
- Demand drop (revenue -15%) w/o adjustments: runway shortens by ~4 months; with Tilt B + selective hiring pause: runway shortens by ~1.5 months.

Unit-economics knobs referenced for product managers (quick list):
- Batching & cache: target 7–12% lower per-token cost with simple defaults; priority for high-throughput customers.
- Routing by policy: shift low-margin traffic to cheaper compatible model variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized model) for specific endpoints.
- Reservation discounts: push customers over threshold to Dedicated with a 20% uplift in committed revenue; reduces blended variable per-token cost materially.

Communication guidance (internal + customer-facing snippet):
- Internal: "We are instituting a temporary pricing tilt to protect service quality and platform sustainability during a period of elevated inference costs. We will re-evaluate weekly and revert when pressures abate."
- Customer: short banner + email for top 5% token customers: emphasize temporary nature, offer Dedicated conversation and usage-efficiency guide.

Open questions / items before exec review:
- Confirm legal/regulatory review for differential pricing by customer segment (Alyssa to confirm).
- Confirm ability for billing system to apply per-key temporary surcharge quickly (SRE/Platform backlog ticket).
- Re-run sensitivity with updated Q2 actual GPU spot data (Marcus to pull).
- Build a one-click dashboard for triggers (SLOs, spot cost, conversion) for Finance + SRE.

Appendix (quick notes on modeling approach):
- Modeled at monthly cadence with simple linear relationships between token volume and variable costs; assume fixed cost pool (infra amortization) unchanged in 3-month window.
- Avoided large headcount reductions in favor of staging to keep go-to-market optionality intact.
- Conservative estimate used for pricing elasticity: top-of-funnel conversion elasticity -8% for a 10% price increase, but high-value Dedicated prospects assumed low elasticity.

If this approach looks directionally correct, next steps:
1) Finance to publish a 3-month cash impact sheet (detailed by team) with two alternative comp assumptions (median and 90th percentile).
2) Platform & Billing to prototype surcharge rollout in staging this week.
3) Product to create a customer messaging draft for the top-5 customers targeted for Tilt B.

Document revision history: Draft created 2025-05-12; updated with SRE feedback 2025-05-28; added legal checklist 2025-06-03.

AUTHORS: Priya Shah (lead), with scenario inputs from Marcus Lee (finance modeling), Alyssa Chen (legal + pricing), Diego Ramirez (platform constraints).
